destinations.name: San Carlos de Bariloche
destinations.highlight: Nahuel Huapi Lake and the Circuito Chico road
destinations.bestSeason: December to March, and July for skiing
destinations.description: Bariloche sits on the southern shore of Nahuel Huapi Lake and is the busiest gateway to the northern Patagonian Andes. The Circuito Chico loop links viewpoints, chairlifts, and beaches within an hour of the town center, and the Cerro Catedral ski area runs from June to September.

destinations.name: Villa La Angostura
destinations.description: A quiet village of wooden houses on the Quetrihue Peninsula. A twelve kilometre trail, walkable or rideable, crosses the peninsula to a rare forest of cinnamon-barked arrayan trees that grows nowhere else at this density.

destinations.name: San Martin de los Andes
destinations.highlight: Lacar Lake and the Seven Lakes Road
destinations.description: The northern end of the Seven Lakes Road, a 110 kilometre paved route through Lanin National Park. The town itself faces Lacar Lake and keeps a strict building code, so every roof in the center is pitched wood and stone.

destinations.name: El Bolson
destinations.highlight: Piltriquitron Mountain and the artisan market
destinations.description: A valley town of small farms, hop fields, and craft breweries between two mountain ranges. The artisan fair fills the main square three days a week, and the trail up Piltriquitron reaches a carved wood forest at 1,400 metres.
destinations.photoCredit: Photo: Marcelo A. Gonzalez, CC BY-SA 4.0

destinations.name: Esquel
destinations.highlight: Los Alerces National Park and La Trochita steam train
destinations.description: Esquel is the base for Los Alerces National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting alerce trees over 2,000 years old. The narrow gauge steam train known as La Trochita still runs tourist services from the town station.

destinations.name: Caviahue and Copahue
destinations.bestSeason: December to March, and July to September for snow
destinations.description: Two small villages on the flank of an active volcano, surrounded by the only araucaria forests in Patagonia. Copahue is known for its sulphur pools and mud baths, which operate as a public spa during the summer months.

destinations.name: El Chalten
destinations.highlight: Mount Fitz Roy and Laguna de los Tres
destinations.description: Argentina's trekking capital, founded in 1985 and built around trailheads rather than roads. Every major hike starts inside the village, including the ten hour round trip to Laguna de los Tres at the base of Fitz Roy.

destinations.name: El Calafate
destinations.description: The town on Argentino Lake that serves Los Glaciares National Park. Perito Moreno is 80 kilometres away and one of the few glaciers in the world that is not retreating; steel walkways face its five kilometre front from a few hundred metres.
destinations.photoCredit: Photo: Luca Galuzzi ( Lucag ), CC BY-SA 2.5

destinations.name: Ushuaia
destinations.highlight: Beagle Channel and Tierra del Fuego National Park
destinations.bestSeason: November to March, and June to September for skiing
destinations.description: The southernmost city in the world, wedged between the Martial range and the Beagle Channel. Catamarans leave the pier daily for sea lion colonies and the Les Eclaireurs lighthouse, and the national park begins twelve kilometres west.
destinations.photoCredit: Photo: Parikshit Sharma Photography, CC BY-SA 4.0

destinations.name: Puerto Madryn
destinations.highlight: Southern right whales in Golfo Nuevo
destinations.description: A coastal city on a sheltered gulf where southern right whales come to breed every winter and spring. Boats leave from Puerto Piramides, and in calm weather the whales can be seen from the shore promenade itself.

destinations.name: Peninsula Valdes
destinations.highlight: Elephant seals, sea lions, and orcas
destinations.description: A UNESCO World Heritage site of gravel roads, salt flats, and cliffs holding one of the largest elephant seal colonies outside Antarctica. Between February and April, orcas hunt sea lion pups at Punta Norte at high tide.

destinations.name: Punta Tombo
destinations.highlight: The largest Magellanic penguin colony on the continent
destinations.description: More than half a million Magellanic penguins nest along three kilometres of this gravel headland between September and March. A raised boardwalk keeps visitors above the burrows while the birds cross freely underneath.

destinations.name: Puerto Deseado
destinations.highlight: The Deseado estuary and Penguin Island
destinations.description: A fishing port on a drowned river valley that shelters Commerson's dolphins, four penguin species, and a colony of rockhopper penguins on Isla Pinguino. Boat trips run from the town pier and last about half a day.

destinations.name: Cueva de las Manos
destinations.highlight: Rock art painted more than 9,000 years ago
destinations.description: Hundreds of stencilled hands cover a rock overhang above the Pinturas River canyon, painted by hunter-gatherer groups over roughly 7,000 years. Access is by guided tour only, from Perito Moreno town or Bajo Caracoles.

destinations.name: Los Antiguos
destinations.highlight: Cherry orchards on Buenos Aires Lake
destinations.description: A green strip of fruit farms on the southern shore of Buenos Aires Lake, the second largest lake in South America. The cherry harvest peaks in January and the town holds a festival for it every summer.

destinations.name: Gaiman and Trelew
destinations.highlight: Welsh tea houses and the Egidio Feruglio dinosaur museum
destinations.description: The Chubut valley was settled by Welsh colonists in 1865 and the language is still taught in local schools. Gaiman keeps the tea house tradition, while Trelew holds the palaeontology museum that described Patagotitan, one of the largest dinosaurs found.

destinations.name: Sarmiento
destinations.description: Trunks up to three metres wide lie where they fell 65 million years ago, turned to stone in a badland of red and grey clay. A marked circuit crosses the reserve, thirty kilometres south of the town on a gravel road.
